findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top convergence gene: pooled UC vs control log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814], up in all eight cohorts. It is mostly local to inflamed mucosa: non-inflamed vs control is only [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399], while the paired inflamed vs non-inflamed change is [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]. CXCR2 is a neutrophil receptor, so the bulk rise likely reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than a change inside the tissue (cell-context check needed); antagonists such as reparixin and navarixin exist.

CXCL8 (IL-8), the ligand of CXCR1 and CXCR2, is strongly and reproducibly up with pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864], in all eight cohorts. It is not quantified in the proteomics study. Its source is largely myeloid and epithelial, so the bulk signal tracks inflammation and neutrophil influx.

MMP3 is up in UC with pooled log2FC [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.901] in all eight cohorts, and the independent proteomics shows the same direction in inflamed mucosa (log2 ratio [gene=MMP3; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.806]), a much smaller protein than RNA change. MMP family members (MMP1, MMP7, MMP10) co-vary, forming a tissue-remodelling signature.

HMGCS2, an epithelial ketogenic metabolism gene, is lost in UC: pooled log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838], down in all eight cohorts, and confirmed at protein level ([gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]). A robust biomarker of epithelial metabolic failure, not a drug target.

SLC26A3 (the genetically linked chloride/bicarbonate exchanger) falls only in inflamed mucosa: paired inflamed vs non-inflamed log2FC [gene=SLC26A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.1781], whereas non-inflamed vs control is unchanged ([gene=SLC26A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0237], padj [gene=SLC26A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.855]). It is a marker of local inflammation, and loss is consistent in all eight cohorts.

CHI3L1 has one of the largest pooled increases, log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875], in all eight cohorts. At protein level the increase is in the same direction but small ([gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607]) and the authors did not call it significant, so RNA effect size overstates the protein change.

IDO1 is induced in UC with pooled log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118] in all eight cohorts, consistent with an IFN-gamma response (tryptophan catabolism); inhibitors exist but the induction is likely a compensatory inflammatory feedback, and immune-cell contribution must be checked.

JAK2 shows a modest but highly significant pooled rise, log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.8744], up in all eight cohorts with high heterogeneity; its rank comes from genetics and tractability more than expression size, and an expression change is not required for JAK inhibitor action.

DUOX2 (with its maturation factor DUOXA2) is among the strongest up genes, pooled log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.412], in all eight cohorts. An epithelial ROS gene, so likely a tissue-intrinsic inflammation/barrier-stress marker rather than immune infiltrate.

AQP8 shows the strongest pooled loss, log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246], significantly down in most cohorts; with CLDN8, PCK1 and GUCA2A/B it forms an epithelial absorptive/metabolic loss signature, a biomarker rather than a target.

caveats: Pooled estimates show very high heterogeneity (I2 about 0.9 for most genes); compare direction and significance across cohorts, not size, as microarray fold changes are compressed.
Bulk expression of neutrophil/myeloid genes (CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCL8, S100A8/9, TREM1, IL1B) is confounded by infiltrating cells; the cell-context specialist must check this.
Proteomics covers a limited protein set; CXCL8 was not quantified, which is not evidence against it.
Only a subset of top genes had paired and protein data checked here.
